title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of Grothendieck's handwritten notes on abelian varieties and cycles. It is a typed page, numbered 25, from a draft of the topos-cohomology material of SGA 4. Its back was evidently reused as scratch paper, which is why it appears upside down in the scan. The surrounding handwritten pages deal with H^1 and the cohomology ring of abelian varieties, cycle maps and duality; this page is unrelated to them.

The content is the end of a Proposition 3.4 and a Definition 3.5. The setting is a topos E (sheaves on a site), a sheaf of rings A, and an A-module F. The proposition states that two conditions are equivalent:
(i) F has no higher cohomology on any object S: H^q(S,F)=0 for all q>0.
(ii) For every epimorphic (covering) family 𝒮=(S_i→S), the Čech cohomology H^q(𝒮,F) vanishes for all q>0.

Proof of (i)⇒(ii): this follows from the exact sequence of Proposition 1.5, the Čech-to-derived comparison. When the higher derived groups vanish on all the fibre products S_{i0}×_S…×_S S_{ik}, the Čech complex computes H^*(S,F), and so it vanishes in positive degrees.

Proof of (ii)⇒(i): fix S and choose a full subcategory C of E with three properties:
- it is small relative to the universe and generates E;
- it is stable under fibre products;
- it contains S.
Give C the induced topology. By the comparison lemma (cited as 3.5.4 of Exposé III), sheaves on C form a topos equivalent to E. The restriction of F to C is then Čech-acyclic for every covering in C (cited as 3.1 and 1.6). By the Cartan–Leray criterion, a sheaf that is Čech-acyclic on all coverings in a generating family stable under fibre products is acyclic. Hence H^q(S,F)=0.

Definition 3.5 names such modules 'acyclic' (or 'E-acyclic'). On a ringed site (C,A), a sheaf of A-modules that is acyclic for the associated topos C̃ is called an acyclic sheaf.

In the published SGA 4 (Exposé V, §4) the same notion is called 'flasque', and the corresponding equivalence appears there as a proposition. The page serves the foundations of cohomology in a topos: it gives a class of modules suitable for computing derived functors and for Čech arguments.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument tacitly uses the Cartan–Leray theorem (Čech-acyclic on a generating family stable under fibre products implies acyclic), which here is hidden behind the references (3.1), (1.6) and Prop. 1.5.
The terminology 'acyclique' differs from the final SGA 4 term 'flasque'. This marks the page as a draft, not an error.

ideas.what: Equivalence between Čech-acyclicity for all coverings and vanishing of higher cohomology for a module on a topos
ideas.modern_name: Flasque modules on a topos; Cartan–Leray acyclicity criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan (for spaces); Grothendieck–Verdier, SGA 4 Exposé V (for topoi)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé V, §4 (flasque modules), where the term is 'flasque' rather than 'acyclique'

ideas.what: Reducing a topos to a small generating full subcategory stable under fibre products, with the induced topology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed draft page of standard SGA 4 foundational material (flasque/acyclic modules on a topos) whose back was reused as scratch paper. Its content is fully published in SGA 4 Exposé V. The only point of mild archival interest is the earlier term 'acyclique' in place of 'flasque' and the different numbering of propositions.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript printed upside down (the back of a reused sheet). It is not part of the handwritten abelian-variety notes on the neighbouring pages.
The '∀' in 'H^q(𝒮,F)=0 ∀ q>0' and in 'H^q(S,F)=0 ∀ q>0' is a handwritten insertion, as the {+∀+} markup indicates.
In (ii), the family is a calligraphic 𝒮=(S_i→S), and the Čech cohomology is written H^q(𝒮,F).
The cross-reference reads '(3.5.4.III)', i.e. 3.5.4 of Exposé III.
